sections.title: Glue code everywhere
body: An API returns users. The dropdown wants {label, value}. So you write a map(). Then the tree wants children, the list wants icons, and the selection callback hands you the reshaped object instead of the one you started with.
sections.caption: A pile of map() calls before anything renders.

sections.title: Data flows in as-is
body: Rokkit’s core pattern is data-first binding: pass your data directly, declare how to read it, and the component adapts. When something is selected, you get back your original object, not a processed copy.
points: Events return the data you passed in
sections.caption: Raw objects slot straight into the list.

sections.title: Bind, don’t convert
body: A list bound to plain state is a single line. The same data can feed a select, a tree or a table.

code.text:
<script>
  import { List } from '@rokkit/ui'
  let items = $state(['a', 'b', 'c'])
  let value = $state(null)
</script>

<List bind:items bind:value />

sections.caption: Selection hands back your original object.

sections.title: Less glue, fewer bugs
body: Generated glue code is where subtle bugs live: a dropped field, a renamed key. Fewer conversions means less code for an assistant to get wrong, and less for you to review.
sections.caption: The reshape step where generated glue breaks.

takeaway: Stop reshaping data for your UI.
